title: Fix escaped characters in iframe srcdoc example
body:
The escaping of quotes in the iframe srcdoc example is, I believe, broken. See the second example in the screenshots below (“nine minutes ago...”). #### Current (broken) #### Proposed (works) ### Checklist - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * n/a - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * n/a - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/master/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chrome: n/a * Firefox: n/a * Safari: n/a ### Process of my first contribution
Some additional notes I found during my initial contribution - `./build.sh` in `html-build` did not ask for a source the first time, it did the second time though - Without Wattsi, there seems to not be highlighting support. The line in `html-build` (“Optionally, for faster builds, you can install Wattsi and Python 2.7 (necessary for applying syntax highlighting to pre contents)”) sounds like Wattsi is used for fast builds, and Python is for highlighting. - I have fpc rev 1: ```sh $ brew install fpc Warning: fpc 3.0.4_1 is already installed and up-to-date ``` ...but `./build.sh` in Wattsi still shows warnings. ```sh $ ./build.sh Writing /Users/tilde/Downloads/oss/wattsi/src/version.inc compile: mode=RELEASE main=wattsi testcmd=bin/wattsi defines=-dUSEROPES -dLINES -dPARSEERROR compile: COMPILING - RELEASE MODE Compiling Release Version Target OS: Darwin for x86_64 ... Linking ../bin/wattsi ld: warning: ld: warning: object file (/usr/local/Cellar/fpc/3.0.4_1/lib/fpc/3.0.4/units/x86_64-darwin/rtl/objpas.o) was built for newer OSX version (10.9) than being linked (10.5)object file (/usr/local/Cellar/fpc/3.0.4_1/lib/fpc/3.0.4/units/x86_64-darwin/rtl/system.o) was built for newer OSX version (10.9) than being linked (10.5) # (many more similar issues like ^) ... 53914 lines compiled, 28.3 sec -rwxr-xr-x 1 tilde staff 1591208 May 25 15:08 ../bin/wattsi executable size: 1591208 bytes compile: Running bin/wattsi wattsi: invalid arguments syntax: wattsi [--quiet] [] wattsi --version real 0m0.008s user 0m0.003s sys 0m0.003s exit value: 0 Removing /Users/tilde/Downloads/oss/wattsi/src/version.inc ``` Worked in the end though!
